question: What determines which implementation of an overridden instance method executes when invoked on a superclass reference variable?

options.text: The actual runtime class of the object instantiated in heap memory.
The declared reference type of the variable assigned at compile time.
The first interface implemented by the superclass in the type hierarchy.
The access visibility specified on the superclass constructor.

explanation: Dynamic method dispatch selects the overriding method implementation based on the runtime type of the object instance, regardless of the reference type.

question: Which of the following members in a Java class does NOT participate in dynamic method dispatch?

options.text: Public instance methods declared inside an abstract superclass.
Overridden instance methods invoked through an interface reference.
Static methods and instance fields, which are resolved statically using reference types.
Protected instance methods overridden in a direct subclass.

explanation: In Java, only non-private instance methods participate in dynamic dispatch; static methods and instance variables are bound at compile time based on reference type.

question: What occurs when a subclass defines a private method with the identical signature to a private method in its superclass?

options.text: The compiler issues a duplicate method declaration error across the hierarchy.
The runtime invokes both methods sequentially during dynamic method lookup.
The subclass method is entirely separate and does not override the superclass method.
The subclass method dynamically overrides the superclass method at runtime.

explanation: Private methods are not visible outside their declaring class and use static binding; a subclass method with the same signature is a new unrelated method.

question: When a reference of declared type `Vehicle` holds an instance of `Car`, which method calls does the compiler permit without casting?

options.text: Only methods defined in Object because polymorphic references mask subclasses.
Only methods returning primitive types across both Vehicle and Car.
Only methods declared in Vehicle or its superclasses, verified at compile time.
Any method declared in Car because dynamic dispatch resolves method bodies at runtime.

explanation: The compiler checks method validity strictly against the compile-time reference type; methods unique to the subclass require an explicit downcast.
